title: SQL Injection login authentication bypass
impact: The login query concatenates the email field directly into a SQL string (SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '<input>' AND password = '<hash>'). Submitting ' OR 1=1-- as the email makes the WHERE clause always true, returning the first user row (the administrator) and issuing a valid admin JWT without knowing any password. This grants full admin account takeover and access to the admin-only /administration panel.
remediation: Use parameterized queries / the ORM's built-in query builder instead of string concatenation for all authentication queries, and validate/escape all user input server-side before it reaches SQL.

title: SQL Injection UNION-based data extraction via product search
payload_used: qwert')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,'1','2','3','4','5','6' FROM Users--
impact: The product search endpoint builds a raw SQL query from the unsanitized q parameter. A UNION SELECT with a matching column count exfiltrates arbitrary table data - here, every user's email address and password hash (MD5) - disguised as product search results. An attacker can dump the entire user table (credentials included) without authentication.
remediation: Use parameterized/prepared statements for the search query, apply strict allow-list input validation on search terms, and never build SQL by string concatenation.

title: Reflected XSS via search query parameter
impact: The search results page reflects the raw q query parameter back into the DOM via an Angular [innerHTML] binding without sanitization. An attacker-crafted link containing an iframe with a javascript: URI executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser as soon as they open the link (e.g. a phished search-results URL), enabling session/token theft or further client-side attacks.
remediation: Sanitize all user-controlled values before binding them with [innerHTML] (or avoid innerHTML entirely and rely on Angular's default text interpolation / DomSanitizer with a strict HTML context), and enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline scripts and javascript: URIs.

title: Stored XSS via login API SQL injection (lastLoginIp)
impact: The same unsanitized login query used for JUICE-001 also allows a UNION SELECT that forges an entire fake user row returned directly in the authentication JWT/response, completely bypassing the normal Sequelize model setters that would otherwise sanitize fields like lastLoginIp. The forged raw HTML is later rendered via an unescaped [innerHTML] binding on the account's Last Login IP page (/#/privacy-security/last-login-ip), executing the attacker's script whenever that page is viewed - a self-stored XSS that shows how a SQLi hole can smuggle persistent XSS past server-side sanitization that only applies to the normal write path.
remediation: Fix the root cause (parameterize the login query) so arbitrary rows can never be forged; additionally sanitize/HTML-encode every field before an [innerHTML] binding regardless of its origin, and never trust data pulled from a raw SQL query result as pre-sanitized.
